title: Delay master task failure notifications until commit

timeline.message:
Delay master task failure notifications until commit

Today when the master service processes a batch of tasks in which some
tasks fail and others succeed, the failure notifications occur straight
away. However, the tasks may have failed because earlier tasks in the
batch succeeded, and the effects of those successful tasks will not be
visible to clients straight away. This commit delays all notifications
until the publication is complete.
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body:
Today when the master service processes a batch of tasks in which some tasks fail and others succeed, the failure notifications occur straight away. However, the tasks may have failed because earlier tasks in the batch succeeded, and the effects of those successful tasks will not be visible to clients straight away. This commit delays all notifications until the publication is complete.

Closes #92677

timeline.body: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
This is debatable, but preserves today's behaviour. Maybe we should return a `FailedToCommitClusterStateException` if the commit failed?

reply.body: Agreed, I think that is the right thing to do, since otherwise, a conflict could still be reported without the offender being committed. Also, I sort of think the failed to commit exception trumps the "application" exception here.

timeline.body: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.
Can we assert that `publishSuccessCountdown.getCount() > 0`? Also in `onSuccess`.

reply.body: I added some checks that tasks are not double-completed in 34e0605cafed1aea283744f2056e7f1af79c730a.

timeline.body: It is not entirely clear to me that this could not be the state returned from the `blockMasterTask`? Perhaps we can pollute the cluster state returned from the real executor with a piece of data to check the presence of?

reply.body: The `blockMasterTask` returns an unchanged state so it isn't published. I added some more machinery to verify this in 34e0605cafed1aea283744f2056e7f1af79c730a.

timeline.body: This looks good. Left a few comments. I think I prefer this approach.
